### Spatial Neighbors Calculation

Options for the calculation of the spatial neighborhood graph.

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--coord_type`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Type of coordinate system. Valid options are:
`grid` - grid coordinates. Only relevant for lattice-based layouts (e.g. Visium). Builds a graph assuming a regular grid topology, where neighbors are defined by grid adjacency rather than distance.
`generic` - Generic coordinates. Recommended for imaging-based data. This option is appropriate for irregularly spaced points, such as cell centroids or spot coordinates from imaging-based assays (e.g. Xenium, CosMx). Setting this option avoids grid-assumption artifacts and ensures each node has spatial neighbors as defined by distance.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"generic"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"generic"`, `"grid"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--n_spatial_neighbors`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Depending on `--coord_type`:
`grid` - number of neighboring tiles.
`generic` - number of neighborhoods for non-grid data. Only used when `--delaunay False`.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `6`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--delaunay`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Whether to use Delaunay triangulation to determine spatial neighborhood graph.
Only used when `--coord_type generic`.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean`

[Default]{.arg-key} `false`
:::
::::
:::::

### NicheCompass Model Architecture

Options for the NicheCompass model architecture.

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--covariate_edges`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
List of booleans that indicate whether there can be edges between different categories of the categorical covariates.
If this is `True` for a specific categorical covariate, this covariate will be excluded from the edge reconstruction loss.
Needs to match the length and order of `--input_obs_covariates`.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `boolean`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--gene_expr_recon_dist`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The distribution used for gene expression reconstruction.
If `nb`, uses a negative binomial distribution.
If `zinb`, uses a zero-inflated negative binomial distribution.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"nb"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"nb"`, `"zinb"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--log_variational`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Whether to transform x by log(x+1) prior to encoding for numerical stability (not for normalization).
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean`

[Default]{.arg-key} `true`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--node_label_method`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Node label method that will be used for omics reconstruction.
If `one-hop-sum`, uses a concatenation of the node's input features with the sum of the input features of all nodes in the node's one-hop neighborhood.
If `one-hop-norm`, uses a concatenation of the node's input features with the node's one-hop neighbors input features normalized as per Kipf, T. N. & Welling, M. Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks. arXiv [cs.LG] (2016).
If `one-hop-attention`, uses a concatenation of the node's input features with the node's one-hop neighbors input features weighted by an attention mechanism.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"one-hop-norm"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"one-hop-norm"`, `"one-hop-sum"`, `"one-hop-attention"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--active_gp_thresh_ratio`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Ratio that determines which gene programs are considered active and are used in the latent representation after model training.
All inactive gene programs will be dropped during model training after a determined number of epochs.
Aggregations of the absolute values of the gene weights of the gene expression decoder per gene program are calculated.
The maximum value, i.e. the value of the gene program with the highest aggregated value will be used as a benchmark and all gene programs whose aggregated value is smaller than `--active_gp_thresh_ratio` times this maximum value will be set to inactive.
If set to 0, all gene programs will be considered active.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0.1`

[Min]{.arg-key} `0.0`

[Max]{.arg-key} `1.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--active_gp_type`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Type to determine active gene programs.
Can be `mixed`, in which case active gene programs are determined across prior and add-on gene programs jointly,
or `separate` in which case they are determined separately for prior and add-on gene programs.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"separate"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"mixed"`, `"separate"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--n_addon_gp`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of addon gene programs (i.e. gene programs that are not included in masks but can be learned de novo).
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `100`

[Min]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--cat_covariates_embeds_nums`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of embedding nodes for all categorical covariates.
Must be the same length as `--input_obs_covariates`.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `integer`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--random_state`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Random seed for reproducibility.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0`

[Min]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline_spatial \
  -r v0.7.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/niche/nichecompass_leiden/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline_spatial/v0.7.0/components/workflows/niche/nichecompass_leiden);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline_spatial \
  -r v0.7.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/niche/nichecompass_leiden/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
